Lululemon is currently navigating a dual challenge of sharp earnings pressure and a major leadership overhaul.

The hedge fund manager sold LULU shares in October for a tax loss.

Burry also increased positions in several other names, including PayPal, MercadoLibre, Adobe, and JD.com.

Famed investor Michael Burry said on Wednesday that he bought back into apparel maker Lululemon Athletica (LULU) after shares fell into the $106 range, framing the move as a bet on temporary neglect rather than permanent damage.

Re-Entry Into Lululemon

Burry cited new management's failure to reverse a prolonged "black hole" in marketing and messaging, which has left the stock overlooked during a low-information stretch. He expressed confidence in the company's research and product development, calling the current price a favorable risk-reward with limited downside and reiterating his June analysis on the stock.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

In a June Substack piece, the hedge fund manager cataloged a history of self-inflicted setbacks at Lululemon due to bad management, and argued that these episodes create value opportunities, while maintaining that the underlying business is not collapsing but is simply stalled. In early October, he sold shares for a tax loss, temporarily swapping into Deckers Outdoor as a proxy with the explicit intention of repurchasing after the wash-sale window.

Lululemon is currently navigating a dual challenge of sharp earnings pressure and a major leadership overhaul. In its second-quarter fiscal 2026 results, revenue fell 4% to $2.4 billion with comparable sales down 9%, while signature leggings sales plunged about 20%. The company cut full-year guidance to a 5–7% revenue decline and EPS of $9.48–$9.73, well below the prior year's $13.26, and warned of a further 10–11% revenue drop in the third quarter.

New CEO Heidi O'Neill, a longtime Nike executive who took the helm in early September, has rapidly restructured the senior team, appointing a new President & Chief Product Officer, Chief Operating Officer, Chief Brand Officer, and Chief Strategy Officer, aiming to refocus the company on product innovation, brand, and execution.

Burry's Other Portfolio Additions

Burry also increased positions in several other names. He bought more MercadoLibre (MELI) shares below $1,500.

"The falling Brazilian real hurts the company's bottom line. It does help to some extent with international competition from Temu, Shein, and Amazon, but not enough. This is why the stock is down, but it has been punished too harshly," Burry said.

MercadoLibre Stock Fell 20% in a Month After Hitting a New 52-Week Low. Is the Selling Overdone?

MercadoLibre Stock Fell 20% in a Month After Hitting a New 52-Week Low. Is the Selling Overdone? ©@small smiles from Getty Images via Canva, @anyaberkut from Getty Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock fell approximately 20% from October 5 to November 10, closing at $1,490.24 after reaching a new 52-week low on November 5.

MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue and financial income rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but operating margin declined to 6.3% as shipping, fulfillment, and marketing investments pressured profitability.

Sea Limited (SE) reported 41.3% revenue growth at Shopee in the third quarter, while Nu Holdings (NU) provides another perspective on Brazilian consumer credit conditions.

MercadoLibre appears potentially undervalued following the selloff, although stronger margins and continued market share gains will be important to a sustained recovery.

What Happened?

MercadoLibre (MELI) stock declined approximately 20% from its October 5 closing price of $1,860.61 to $1,490.24 on November 10, after hitting a new 52-week low on November 5.

The decline reflects two concerns: political uncertainty in Brazil and weaker-than-expected profitability despite strong revenue growth.

Brazil's October 25 presidential runoff delivered another term for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defeated Flávio Bolsonaro after trailing him in the first round.

MercadoLibre shares fell approximately 8% on October 26 as investors reassessed Brazil's economic outlook, currency risks, and consumer spending conditions.

Brazil generated approximately $15.2 billion of MercadoLibre's $28.9 billion in 2025 revenue, making it the company's largest market.

However, the company's third-quarter earnings report created a more immediate concern.

According to MercadoLibre's third-quarter financial results, revenue and financial income increased 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, but reported earnings of $8.83 per share fell short of the $9.27 consensus estimate cited in the initial research brief.

Operating margin declined to 6.3% from approximately 9.8% a year earlier, reflecting higher shipping expenses, expanded fulfillment capacity, and increased marketing spending in Brazil.

In its third-quarter shareholder letter, management described the pressure on shipping margins as "the price of the habit we set out to build."

The strategy is producing results. Items sold in Brazil increased more than 40% year over year for the fifth consecutive quarter, while MercadoLibre gained market share across its three largest markets.

Its lower free-shipping threshold also encouraged smaller purchases, initially putting pressure on shipping economics.

By September, Brazilian orders valued between R$19 and R$79 that qualified for free or slower delivery became variable contribution-positive for the first time, suggesting higher order volumes are beginning to improve shipping economics.

Competition remains significant.

Sea Limited's third-quarter results showed Shopee revenue increased 41.3% to approximately $6.1 billion, highlighting the continued growth of a major e-commerce rival.

Shopee's expansion increases the importance of MercadoLibre retaining customers and improving logistics efficiency in Brazil.

Meanwhile, Nu Holdings reported a 4.8% early-stage nonperforming loan ratio in the second quarter, providing another indicator of consumer credit conditions as Brazilian economic uncertainty increases.

MercadoLibre's 15-to-90-day nonperforming loan ratio remained around 7.0% in the third quarter, broadly stable from the prior quarter and a year earlier.

For long-term investors, the central question is whether higher purchasing frequency and growing shipment volumes can eventually offset near-term margin pressure.

Is MercadoLibre Stock Undervalued or Overvalued?

MercadoLibre appears potentially undervalued following its recent decline, although its earnings recovery remains uncertain.

According to TIKR's November 2 consensus snapshot, normalized earnings per share were projected to rise from $38.26 in 2026 to $55.89 in 2027, representing approximately 46% growth.

MercadoLibre (MELI): normalized EPS, actual and consensus estimates, $ per share, fiscal 2024-2029 (TIKR)

These forecasts preceded the latest earnings report, meaning analysts could revise expectations if shipping and fulfillment investments continue weighing on profitability.

MercadoLibre traded at approximately 41x forward earnings on November 2, compared with its five-year average of roughly 63x.

MercadoLibre (MELI): forward (NTM) P/E, last 5 years (TIKR)

However, the five-year average includes unusually high valuations during 2021, making it an imperfect benchmark for assessing fair value today.

Over the next 12 months, MercadoLibre's investment case will depend on improving fulfillment utilization, lower shipping costs per order, sustained e-commerce growth, and stable credit quality.

Higher shipment volumes could help spread fulfillment expenses across more orders, allowing revenue growth to translate into stronger operating margins.

If these improvements materialize, MercadoLibre could deliver meaningful earnings growth and justify a higher valuation.

Conversely, persistent margin pressure, intensifying competition from Shopee, or weaker Brazilian consumer spending could trigger additional earnings-estimate cuts.

Overall, the recent selloff appears potentially overdone given MercadoLibre's strong revenue growth and continued market share gains. However, sustained upside will likely require evidence that its investments are translating into stronger profitability.

Key Takeaways

MercadoLibre stock fell 10% in the week to Nov. 10 after third-quarter EPS came in at $8.83, short of the $9.27 analysts expected, even as revenue rose 45%.

Management chose the squeeze, spending on free shipping and warehouses while Sea Limited's Shopee keeps gaining in Brazil.

Brazil's cost per shipment is falling, and credit held steady, a bar for Nu Holdings ahead of its expected Nov. 12 report.

Analysts still expect an earnings rebound, and the stock trades far below its usual forward multiple.

MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ) stock fell 10% from Nov. 3 to Nov. 10, with most of the damage in a 12% drop on Nov. 5, the day after its report. Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but EPS of $8.83 missed the $9.27 expected.

That spending comes as Shopee, owned by Sea Limited (SE:NYSE), pushes harder in Brazil, which Sea said on Nov. 10 was again its fastest-growing market. And MercadoLibre's credit sets a bar for Nu Holdings (NU:NYSE), which is expected to report on Nov. 12.

The miss was a choice

Operating income fell 6.6% to $676 million, a 6.3% margin against 9.8% a year earlier. The company paid for more free shipping, added fulfillment space ahead of the holidays and stepped up affiliate marketing in Brazil. CEO Ariel Szarfsztejn told analysts the company is spending because the opportunity in front of it is large. "We have accepted a lower margin to do that," he said.

But the shipping bill is starting to shrink: Brazil's cost per shipment fell 5% from a year earlier in local currency. And in September, orders between R19andR79, which now ship free, paid their own variable costs for the first time.

Shopee is pushing just as hard. It launched four-hour delivery in greater São Paulo in August with more than 4,000 partner stores, and Sea said on Nov. 10 that the service now runs from more than 7,000. MercadoLibre began testing one-hour delivery in parts of the city in September. Sea also said Shopee again grew faster than Brazil's broader market in the third quarter.

title: Did The Market Read eBay Stock Right?
detail:
Did The Market Read eBay Stock Right?
Trefis Team
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 6:34 PM MST 3 min read

WMT
MELI
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

For questions about this article or underlying research, email help@trefis.com.

eBay (EBAY) stock rose 53.7% from February 12 to November 9, 2026, while the S&P 500 returned 11.4%. Over that stretch the company put out four quarterly reports, the last on October 28, and on July 30 it completed its purchase of Depop, a fashion marketplace. How much faster is eBay growing than it was a year ago? The market's read of eBay turns on that, and on whether faster sales lift profit per share, which has barely moved.

eBay's Sales Grew Much Faster Than A Year Earlier

Over the four quarters to September 30, 2026, which are the four eBay reported during the rise, revenue grew 15.7% to $12.4 billion. That is more than three times the 4.4% growth of the four quarters before. Third-quarter revenue alone grew 13.7%, against 9.5% a year earlier, so growth stayed faster than a year before, though below the 15.7% for the four quarters.

How Much Of eBay's Growth Came From Depop?

Depop accounted for a slice of that growth, not most of it. During the October 28 call, management said third-quarter revenue grew 13% excluding currency swings, and that Depop added nearly 2 points of it.

Management expects slower growth in the fourth quarter, forecasting revenue between $3.19 billion and $3.24 billion. Excluding Depop and currency swings, the company projects growth of 5% to 7%, compared with 11% in the third quarter. Management said its fourth-quarter outlook for gross merchandise volume, the value of goods sold on eBay, reflects a very strong quarter a year earlier that was helped in part by trading cards and bullion. The company also expects growth in trading cards to moderate in 2027.

eBay Earned About The Same Per Share

Profit per share did not track the rise in sales. eBay earned $4.58 per share over the four quarters to September 30, 2026, compared with $4.57 a year earlier. Operating income rose with sales, but net income slipped.

Investors are therefore paying more for the same profit per share. At the November 9 close, eBay traded at 25.6 times past-year earnings, compared with 21.8 times for the S&P 500. The stock traded at 19.1 times at the end of September 2025. The current price appears to assume that faster sales will start to show up in profit per share. So far the faster sales are real, but profit per share has not yet followed.

One part of eBay's case has held up over the year, though it slipped in the latest quarter: the share of each sales dollar it keeps as operating profit. Its operating margin was 20.3% over the four quarters to September 30, 2026, against 20.6% a year earlier. In the third quarter alone it was 19.2%, against 20.2% in the third quarter of 2025. When eBay next reports, expected in February 2027, the figures to watch are its operating margin and its profit per share, since net income slipped even as operating income rose.

MercadoLibre has 31% upside to analysts' average target, but its operating margin slipped to 6.3% in the third quarter.

Danaher looks like the best buy of the three, as the only one with a higher average analyst target than a year ago.

Eagle Capital Management, a fund that manages $35.8 billion, made its three biggest adds of the second quarter to MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ), Danaher (DHR:NYSE) and S&P Global (SPGI:NYSE), according to its 13F for the quarter ended June 30, filed Aug. 14.

That filing is still its latest. Since June, two of the three have climbed hard, and over the past year analysts have raised their average target on just one of them.

MercadoLibre is the biggest bet of the three

The fund raised its MercadoLibre stake 79% in the second quarter, to 1.41 million shares worth $2.39 billion at June 30. That's 7.3% of its 13F stocks and its No. 3 position, and the stock is up 3% since.

MercadoLibre reported its third quarter on Nov. 4, and it was more of the same. Revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion. But operating income fell 6% to $676 million, and the operating margin slipped to 6.3%, from 6.7% in the second quarter and 9.8% a year earlier. The company said the drop came from more free shipping, new fulfillment capacity ahead of its peak season and "a tactical decision to increase affiliate marketing spend in Brazil."

The bulls were counting on profit growth, and they didn't get it. Analysts have been lowering their sights all year, too. Their consensus target is down 21% over the past year, to $2,272 from $2,877:

Shares of MercadoLibre, Inc. MELI have plunged 11.9% since the company reported third-quarter 2026 results on Nov. 4, reflecting investor concerns over profitability despite robust revenue growth and continued expansion across its commerce and fintech businesses. The sell-off highlights concerns about the company's aggressive investments in logistics, customer acquisition and financial services, which are supporting engagement but weighing on near-term margins.

Over the past three months, MELI shares have lost 16%, underperforming the industry, the Zacks Retail – Wholesale sector and the S&P 500's decline of 8.7%, 3.1% and 5.7%, respectively. The stock has also lagged Amazon.com, Inc. AMZN, which has dipped 3.6% over the same period. However, MELI has performed better than Sea Limited SE, which has tumbled 31.2%.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

With the stock experiencing significant selling pressure, investors face a key question: Does the recent correction present an attractive entry opportunity, or do persistent margin headwinds warrant caution?

MELI's Q3 Results: What Triggered the Sell-Off?

MercadoLibre reported strong third-quarter 2026 revenue growth, but profitability pressures overshadowed its top-line performance. Net revenues and financial income rose 45% year over year to $10.75 billion, reflecting sustained commerce and fintech momentum. However, income from operations declined 6% to $676 million, while operating margin contracted to 6.3% from 9.8% a year earlier and 6.7% in the preceding quarter.

Net income increased 6% to $448 million, although net margin narrowed to 4.2% from 5.7% year over year. Earnings per share of $8.83 missed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $9.41, adding to investor concerns.

Margin compression primarily reflected higher shipping costs, fulfillment investments and marketing expenses. Net shipping costs created a 60-basis-point sequential margin headwind as lower free-shipping thresholds encouraged smaller, more frequent purchases. Fulfillment capacity expanded nearly 20% sequentially ahead of peak demand, while elevated energy prices increased transportation expenses.

Meanwhile, increased affiliate marketing investments in Brazil pushed sales and marketing expenses up 40 basis points sequentially to 11.6% of revenues. Higher provisions associated with credit portfolio growth also added to year-over-year profitability pressures.

Although these investments aim to strengthen customer engagement and long-term growth, their near-term earnings impact and uncertainty surrounding margin recovery appear to have contributed to the stock's decline.
